unitTitles.4: Statistical inference: bivariate data and other procedures

toolsSub: The things you will reach for in every unit.

thinking.title: Statistical thinking: the big ideas
thinking.lead: Statistics is a way of thinking about the world wherever data, variation, and chance appear. It is more than a math requirement. It helps you question claims, not only calculate answers.

habits.title: Question the claim
habits.text: Who collected the data, how, and who is missing? Spotting bias is the first statistical skill.

habits.title: Expect variation
habits.text: No two samples are alike. Statistics asks what chance alone would produce before it asks what is surprising.

habits.title: Decide with evidence
habits.text: Probability and evidence let us make informed decisions without pretending to be certain.

thinking.doTitle: Two things you will be able to do well
do: Read a graph of data and say what it shows, and what it does not.
Take a statistical claim, run the right procedure, and write a conclusion that answers the claim.
thinking.closing: Data also shapes equity, culture, identity, and opportunity. Behind every dataset are people, and good statistical thinking keeps them in view.

paths.title: I do not understand the idea
paths.text: Watch a micro-lecture for the outcome, then read the FAQ for your unit.

paths.title: I do not know how to start
paths.text: Use a procedure helper to choose the method. Then follow the steps in the Art of Stat guide.

paths.title: My technology is not working
paths.text: The Art of Stat guide has menu paths and a video for each task. A scientific calculator covers the rest.

paths.title: I got it wrong and do not know why
paths.text: Use an AI study partner to find the first place your thinking went off track. Or ask your class and say exactly where you got stuck.

paths.title: I am behind or overwhelmed
paths.text: You do not have to sort it out alone. Talk to a person, or ask for help with basic needs.

ai.title: AI study partner
ai.sub: Use AI after you have tried the problem. Pick a mode, copy the prompt, fill in the brackets, and paste it into Gemini, Claude, or ChatGPT.

modes.title: Explain it
modes.text: After you have tried the problem, get a plain-language explanation and one check question.
modes.prompt: I am learning [topic] in my introductory statistics class. I already tried the problem on my own. Explain the idea in plain language with one everyday analogy, then ask me one question to check that I understood.

modes.title: Coach me
modes.text: Get questions and small hints, one step at a time, never the final answer.
modes.prompt: Act as a Socratic statistics tutor. Here is my problem: [paste problem]. Do not give me the answer or do the calculations. Ask me one question at a time, and give a small hint only when I am stuck.

modes.title: Check my thinking
modes.text: Paste your work and find the first step where your reasoning goes off track.
modes.prompt: Here is a problem and my work: [paste problem and your steps]. Do not solve it for me. Find the first step where my reasoning goes wrong, explain why, and let me fix it myself.

S12.title: The mistake to watch for
S12.text: When the question is about a sample mean, divide σ by √n. "What is the probability of a result higher than 55?" is about one value. "A sample of 5 scores is collected. What is the probability the mean is higher than 55?" is about a sample mean, so it needs σ/√n.
